page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Each core supports hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highmem-4 in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (1109.89) and multi-core (2914.17) CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, reflecting older architectural limitations. Cryptographic and compression tasks also register lower-tier results, with a Geekbench single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 2032.0. Redis SET operations achieve 2.75 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.82 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a cost-effective profile for legacy or non-critical workloads requiring a higher memory footprint without demanding high-performance compute capabilities. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable execution, though the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a performance tradeoff compared to newer generations. This instance is best suited for moderate database caching, memory-bound utility scripts, lightweight web serving, and development environments where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
